# Code Map — Budgeting (Zero-Based Budgeting Console)

Next.js 16 / React 19, Owner/Accountant only. The design system (ui/, theme.ts,
globals.css, NavRail, HeaderClock) is a **verbatim copy of Dispatcher** — change Dispatcher
first, then re-copy; never edit the copy in place. Manifest + drift check: Budgeting/CLAUDE.md.

## Screens — Budgeting/components/screens (7 top-level)
<!-- gen:budgeting-screens:start -->
| Screen | ~Lines |
|---|---|
| ActualsVsBudget.tsx | ~500 |
| BudgetCodes.tsx | ~700 |
| BudgetPeriods.tsx | ~100 |
| Reports.tsx | ~100 |
| Settings.tsx | ~200 |
| Variance.tsx | ~200 |
| shared.tsx | ~200 |
Sub-screen folders: screens/periods/ (5)
<!-- gen:budgeting-screens:end -->
<!-- notes:budgeting-screens:start -->
- BudgetPeriods.tsx is two modes in one screen, chosen by openPeriodId (hoisted into Console, so stepping over to Budget Codes and back keeps your place): a full-width list of periods, or one period taking over the whole content area — that dashboard and its parts live in screens/periods/ (PeriodList, PeriodDashboard, LifecycleStepper, PlanningChecklist, one AllocationSection per code category). Allocation lines exist only inside a period now; the flat Allocations.tsx screen is gone, and there is no master/detail split any more.
- ActualsVsBudget.tsx is real (GET periods/{id}/rollup for the per-code comparison, periods/{id}/actuals for the transactions behind it) and owns the two things the server deliberately omits: the variance bands (varianceKind/varianceLabel in lib/data.ts) and the revenue/expense split. Variance.tsx is the last mock screen in the console.
- After a transition or line save, the dashboard refetches the projection until the expected state/values appear (`stateAfter`) before refreshing the period list — reads are eventually consistent.
- BudgetCodes.tsx groups the list by cost centre case-folded for display only (lib/api/budgeting.ts groupBudgetCodesByCostCentre: `Fleet`/`FLEET` share a group, but the server stores exact spellings and nothing merges them); revenue codes get their own bucket, not "No cost centre".
<!-- notes:budgeting-screens:end -->

## Components — Budgeting/components
<!-- gen:budgeting-components:start -->
app/: globals.css, layout.tsx, page.tsx
Top-level: AccessDeniedScreen, ActualTransactionFormModal, AuthGate, Brandmark, BudgetAllocationFormModal, BudgetCodeFormModal, BudgetPeriodFormModal, Console, ErrorNotice, HeaderClock, LoginScreen, NavRail, ProfileForm.test, ProfileForm, RoleGate.test, RoleGate, SetupPendingScreen, TopBar
ui/ (12): Button, Chip, CorridorStepper, Field, FileField, ImageUploadField, MetricTile, ModalShell, MonthGrid, Pager, Panel, PeriodNav
<!-- gen:budgeting-components:end -->
<!-- notes:budgeting-components:start -->
- RoleGate enforces the Owner/Accountant client-side gate (UX only — the security boundary is the gateway BudgetAccess policy on /api/budgeting).
- ActualTransactionFormModal makes two server rules visible instead of letting a 409 teach them: the date must fall inside an existing period (it names which one while you pick, since no period id is stored) and new spend cannot go on a retired code, though a row already sitting on one stays correctable.
<!-- notes:budgeting-components:end -->

## Lib — Budgeting/lib (22 files)
<!-- gen:budgeting-lib:start -->
api/ (7): budgeting, budgeting.test, format, identity, identity.test, shared, transport
Top-level: auth, claims.test, claims, clipboard, data, format, money.test, money, nav, period, roles.test, roles, theme, types, useToday
<!-- gen:budgeting-lib:end -->
<!-- notes:budgeting-lib:start -->
- api/budgeting.ts is the real API wiring — periods, codes, allocations AND actual transactions all come from the backend; data.ts now keeps only the mock variance rows (plus the budgetCodes lookup feeding them and Reports' revenue mix), alongside varianceKind/varianceLabel, which are not mock: the real Actuals vs Budget screen reads the bands from there.
- api/identity.ts is the one client here that calls a non-budgeting endpoint (Identity's /api/identity/auth/profile, feeding components/ProfileForm.tsx in the Settings Profile tab); its PUT sends the whole profile, so an omitted field clears rather than preserves.
<!-- notes:budgeting-lib:end -->
